editorialRead.readHeadline: QwenLM/qwen-code is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: QwenLM/qwen-code leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 24 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 24 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: QwenLM/qwen-code — 3 commits today and 1 same-day mapped article, 37.7 below its current daily pace, with 6 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
openclaw/openclaw — 42 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
Kilo-Org/kilocode — No same-day commit after 278 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Test the restore path, not just the fork policy
dailyInsight.insight: Qwen Code’s fresh fork allowlist supports one bounded, project-scoped test: if a parent uses `fork_tools` to narrow a background child, stop and verify the restriction after the child is revived, not only at launch. The public implementation keeps an empty list as deny-all, rejects a forbidden call before construction or approval, stores the policy in fork metadata, and reapplies it to the current parent-derived registry when the fork resumes.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The new optional `fork_tools` parameter leaves model-visible declarations intact while applying a separate execution gate. Exact tool names and bounded MCP patterns can be allowed; unknown names fail closed by matching nothing; and a denied call receives a synthetic response before it can construct a tool, trigger a hook, classify permissions, schedule, or ask for approval. On cold revival, the current system instruction and tool registry are rebound while the launch-time allowlist is restored from the persisted sidecar.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A policy that exists only in the launch request is not a reliable delegated-work boundary. An agent can resume after a parent changes tools, reconnects MCP servers, or replaces context. Testing the restored gate turns an attractive configuration feature into an observable recovery invariant.

actions.audience: Qwen Code operator or integrator using background fork subagents
actions.label: Run one deny-all-and-resume drill
actions.instruction: In an isolated test workspace, launch a fork with `fork_tools: []`, attempt one harmless built-in tool call, then stop and revive the fork. Verify before and after revival that the call is rejected before an approval prompt or tool hook is reached. Repeat with one explicitly allowed read-only tool, and record which parent runtime supplied the policy. Do not treat a passing result as a filesystem or administrator sandbox guarantee.

receipts.title: Add fork tool execution allowlist (#8066)
receipts.supports: Shows the fork-only policy, deny-all semantics, pre-construction denial, persisted executionAllowedTools metadata, current-registry revival, and focused tests.

confidence.basis: One fresh, directly inspected Qwen Code commit contains both the documented boundary and implementation tests for launch, denial, persistence, and background revival.

dailyInsight.limitation: This is source-level Qwen Code evidence. It does not establish a released build, behavior across every CLI, desktop, daemon, or IDE surface, or an administrator-enforced sandbox. The design explicitly says the parent model or caller supplies the policy.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise this call if a public regression shows a forbidden tool can be constructed, approved, or executed after a restricted fork revives, if an empty list regains wildcard behavior, or if the project changes the documented parent-supplied boundary.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for public end-to-end resumed-fork tests across MCP reconnects and for a project-controlled policy layer that can enforce the same restriction independently of a parent model’s request.
